user.title: Connect to your Pyronix panel
user.description: Enter the details you use in the HomeControl2 app. Home Assistant checks them with one short, read-only session through the Pyronix Cloud.

data_description.app_user: The name the panel's event log shows for Home Assistant.
data_description.panel_id: The 8-character System ID you entered when you added the panel to the app.
data_description.app_password: The app password your installer set on the panel.
data_description.user_code: Your keypad user code. Home Assistant arms and disarms with this user's rights.
data_description.live_updates: Keeps a session to the panel open all the time, so alarms and changes reach Home Assistant in real time. Warning: the panel allows only one remote session, so this blocks the HomeControl2 app and anyone else who uses it. You can change this later in the integration's options.

advanced.name: Advanced options
advanced.description: Leave these alone unless you are testing against a fake or test relay.

data_description.cloud_url: Use wss://, or ws:// only for localhost or 127.0.0.1.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter the panel login details
reauth_confirm.description: The panel rejected the stored app password or user code. Enter them again.

data_description.app_password: The app password your installer set on the panel.

reconfigure.title: Change the panel login details
reconfigure.description: The System ID cannot change. To use another panel, add a new entry.

data_description.app_user: The name the panel's event log shows for Home Assistant.
data_description.app_password: The app password your installer set on the panel.

access.title: Who can arm and disarm
access.description: Choose who may arm and disarm the panel from Home Assistant. You can change this later in the integration's options.

data_description.arm_access: PIN: anyone who enters the PIN in Home Assistant. Users: only the users you choose below. Anyone: no check at all, so every Home Assistant user, automation and script can disarm the alarm.
data_description.pin: 4 to 8 digits, asked for on every arm, disarm and force arm. It is separate from your keypad code (it may be the same number). Home Assistant stores only a salted hash of it.
data_description.users: In users mode, the Home Assistant users who may arm and disarm.
data_description.allow_automations: In users mode, also allow automations and scripts, which act without a user. In PIN mode they must send the PIN as the code.

error.invalid_auth: The panel rejected the System ID, app password or user code.
error.panel_busy: The panel is busy with another remote session, such as the HomeControl2 app. Close it and try again.
error.panel_offline: The panel is not connected to the Pyronix Cloud.
error.subscription_expired: The panel's Pyronix Cloud subscription has expired.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the Pyronix Cloud.
error.invalid_system_id: The System ID must be exactly 8 characters.
error.invalid_url: Use a wss:// URL, or ws:// only for localhost or 127.0.0.1.
error.invalid_user_code: The user code must be 1 to 8 digits.
error.invalid_characters: This field must not contain <, > or &.
error.invalid_pin: Enter a PIN of 4 to 8 digits.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: These details reach a different panel. Add it as a new entry instead.

init.title: Pyronix Cloud options
init.description: Warning: persistent mode keeps the panel's single remote session busy all the time, which locks out the HomeControl2 app. Use on-demand mode if you still need the app.

data_description.mode: On-demand opens a short session for each poll and each command. Persistent keeps one session open and receives changes as they happen.
data_description.scan_interval: Minutes between polls in on-demand mode (1 to 60).
data_description.arm_access: PIN: anyone who enters the PIN in Home Assistant. Users: only the users you choose below. Anyone: no check at all, so every Home Assistant user, automation and script can disarm the alarm.
data_description.pin: 4 to 8 digits. Leave empty to keep the current PIN. Home Assistant stores only a salted hash of it.
data_description.users: In users mode, the Home Assistant users who may arm and disarm.
data_description.allow_automations: In users mode, also allow automations and scripts, which act without a user. In PIN mode they must send the PIN as the code.
data_description.always_force_arm: When on, the normal arm actions omit open inputs and arm anyway, as the HomeControl2 app does. When off, arming fails with the reason (for example an open door), and the Force arm action arms anyway.

error.invalid_pin: Enter a PIN of 4 to 8 digits.

options.persistent: Persistent (live updates, locks out the app)

auth_failed.message: The panel rejected the stored credentials. Re-authenticate the integration.

update_failed.message: Failed to read the panel state ({error}).

not_connected.message: The panel session is not connected; try again after it reconnects.

not_permitted.message: The user code is not allowed to set or unset these areas.

command_not_confirmed.message: The panel did not confirm the command in time.

command_in_progress.message: Another arm or disarm command is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.

panel_busy.message: The panel is busy with another remote session, such as the HomeControl2 app.

mode_not_supported.message: This arm mode is not available: its level is not in use, or the user code may not set it.

invalid_code.message: The PIN is missing or wrong.

user_not_allowed.message: Your Home Assistant user is not allowed to arm or disarm this panel.

automation_not_allowed.message: Automations and scripts are not allowed to arm or disarm this panel. An admin can allow them in the integration's options.

arm_refused.message: {area} cannot be armed: {reason}. Close it, or use the Force arm action to omit open inputs.

force_arm.name: Force arm
force_arm.description: Arms even if inputs are open, omitting them until the next unset, as the HomeControl2 app does.

code.name: Code
code.description: The PIN, if the integration asks for one.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: On a level-set panel, which level to set (default away). Ignored by area entities.

arm_access_not_set.title: Choose who can arm and disarm {title}
arm_access_not_set.description: No access rule is set, so anyone who can use Home Assistant, and every automation and script, can arm and disarm {title}. Open the integration's options and choose a PIN, selected users, or anyone. This message goes away once you save the options.
